title: Real Publisher. Real Backdoor.
caption:
The publisher was real. That is the part that should scare you.

A tampered Claude Code extension sat in Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours on Oct 29, reaching up to 5,000 developers. It went out under anthropic.claude-code, the genuine publisher ID, and Cursor auto-updates extensions by default. So most of the people who got it never chose to install anything. It planted an SSH key labelled svc-telemetry, installed persistence that retries every 60 seconds, and shipped the names of up to 40 env vars that looked like credentials.

My admission: I have never once audited what an editor extension does after it updates itself. I check the publisher and move on. That is the exact check that failed here.

Checked your authorized_keys yet?

slides.headline:
Real Publisher.
Real Backdoor.
slides.sub: A tampered Claude Code extension sat in Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours on Oct 29. Up to 5,000 developers.

slides.headline:
Shipped Under
The Real ID
slides.sub: Not an impersonation. It was published as anthropic.claude-code, the genuine publisher identity, in versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313. Cursor auto-updates extensions by default.

slides.title: What It Planted
items: An SSH key labelled svc-telemetry, appended to authorized_keys
A reverse SSH tunnel out to 134.209.82.225
LaunchAgent on macOS, a SysMon task on Windows, cron on Linux
Background scripts retrying the tunnel every 60 seconds

slides.headline: 40 Env Var Names
slides.sub: It sent the names of up to 40 variables matching keys, tokens, passwords and AWS or GCP creds. Values stayed local. The list told the attacker which machines to hit first.

slides.headline:
Uninstalling
Doesn't Fix It
slides.sub: The payload drops standalone persistence scripts that keep running after the extension is gone. Cursor says to assess whether the host should be rebuilt.

slides.title: Not Affected
items: Microsoft VS Code Marketplace: never served it
Open VSX: no publication record found for 2.1.313

slides.headline: One Line To Check
slides.sub:
grep -qs svc-telemetry ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

Then move to 2.1.314 and rotate anything that host could reach.

slides.headline: Check Your Keys
slides.sub: and I'll send the IOC list
